output.name: Lanthir — The Lantern Boat
output.myth: When Aun cut the string he did not know that a sky has weight, and Tavo the Gale came in under the drift and lifted the first boats off the water. Ennu the Kite-Wright sewed a boat for Lanthir from sailcloth and whale rib, and sent her after Aun's loose sky. Lanthir went down the Leeward shelves with her mast bent and her sail full of the wrong wind. Past the skerries where the drowned stand with their arms held out, as shags dry their wings, she did not stop. Tavo laughed and laughed, then let her run south toward the Turned Wake, where the water tilts under anyone who sails far enough. She did not come home. Kael the Netter casts for her in the south, his net full of cold light, and has never hauled up more than a spark of her lamp. Old women say that on a black night, from a boat's stern, you may see the low star where the mast meets the water, and her lantern swinging. Do not wave. Tavo is watching the same star.
output.finding: From Thavesk, the Turned Wake, look one fist north along the sky and you will find Lanthir, her lamp low over the Leeward water.
